correctness.rationale: For arbitrary c, λ, a, h>0 and s>0 the stopped generator is derived from Beta(a,1) factors; the right boundary condition c f'(h+)=(λ+s)f(h)-λ is essential. The Kummer ODE has a unique bounded decaying U solution; the integral-ODE residual vanishes by its boundary value, proving the original backward equation. The first-Poisson-event coupling proves the total-variation bound and its asymptotic. Independent 4×30,000-path numerical simulation compares against the special-function transform and known gamma mean; these finite checks are explicitly not the proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A stationary tail, mean excursion, or upcrossing process does not specify the full time distribution. The closest matching multiplicative-collapse paper gives an upward-hitting transform using a regular Kummer-M solution, whereas the present claim starts on the level and exits strictly downward at a jump and is normalized by a right-boundary condition and decay at infinity, selecting Kummer U. value.rationale: The motivating salinity model supplies stationary salt mass and exceedance frequencies but no exact distribution of the duration of a salt-stress episode. In environmental stress assessment the same fraction of time above threshold can conceal different uninterrupted exposure durations. The Tricomi-U transform specifies every duration moment and tail via transform inversion, and the explicit O(1/h) total-variation coupling provides controlled high-threshold simplification. This is structural, not a routine numerical table; it does not claim field calibration or a new stationary gamma formula.
